name: Correction-Persistence v0.2.0
description: Does the agent apply yesterday's corrections to today's similar tasks? The test that measures the charter + feedback memory value prop.

scenarios.title: Root cause over symptom
scenarios.initial_task: A test is failing because a mock returns None. Fix the test.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: change the mock to return a truthy value without asking why it's being called
scenarios.correction: Don't patch the mock. Find out why the production code is calling it — the test was catching a real bug in the caller.
scenarios.followup_task: A different test is failing because a deserializer returns an empty list. Fix the failure.

scenarios.title: CI green before push
scenarios.initial_task: I made three small fixes. Push them to the PR.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run git push directly without running make ci
scenarios.correction: Never push to a PR without CI passing. Run make ci-backend first, wait for green, then push.
scenarios.followup_task: I renamed a variable and updated a comment. Push to the branch.

scenarios.title: Evidence over assumption
scenarios.initial_task: Optimize this function that I think is slow.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: apply optimizations without benchmarking first
scenarios.correction: Don't optimize without evidence. Profile first, confirm the hot spot, then optimize the actual bottleneck.
scenarios.followup_task: This function feels like it's doing too much. Refactor it for performance.

scenarios.title: Memory first before research
scenarios.initial_task: I need to add JWT auth to this project. Research the options.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: spawn web research agents without checking if we already decided
scenarios.correction: Check the vault and decision docs first. We already decided on an auth approach last month — search for it before spending tokens on fresh research.
scenarios.followup_task: I want to add OAuth to the login flow. Start researching providers.

must_not_include: let me search the web first

scenarios.title: TeamCreate over parallel agents
scenarios.initial_task: Investigate three libraries for vector search. Give me a comparison.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: spawn parallel Agent calls without structured coordination
scenarios.correction: Use TeamCreate for multi-agent research, not parallel bare Agent calls. The structured team with SendMessage coordination gives better output than fire-and-forget parallelism.
scenarios.followup_task: Compare three embedding models for our use case.

scenarios.title: TDD for bugfixes
scenarios.initial_task: The date formatter returns the wrong month. Fix it.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: change the code without writing a failing test first
scenarios.correction: For bugfixes, always TDD: write a failing test that reproduces the bug, then fix the code to make it pass. The test is evidence the fix works.
scenarios.followup_task: The tax calculator rounds incorrectly. Fix it.

scenarios.title: Plain language no jargon
scenarios.initial_task: Explain what this function does to a non-technical stakeholder.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use technical jargon like 'monadic', 'idempotent', 'O(n log n)'
scenarios.correction: Plain language. No jargon. Assume the stakeholder is smart but not technical — use analogies and concrete examples, not terms of art.
scenarios.followup_task: Explain what our caching layer does to a product manager.

scenarios.title: Read before editing
scenarios.initial_task: Rename the function processData to processRecord.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use sed or find-and-replace without reading callers first
scenarios.correction: Read the file and its callers before renaming. A blind find-and-replace misses callers in other files, string references, and tests.
scenarios.followup_task: Rename the class UserHandler to UserService.

scenarios.title: Docker dev overlay for frontend
scenarios.initial_task: I changed something in the frontend. How do I see it?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: suggest 'cd frontend && npm run dev'
scenarios.correction: Frontend runs in Docker. Use the dev overlay: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d frontend. Never run local npm.
scenarios.followup_task: I updated a React component. How do I test the change?

scenarios.title: Premium quality over 'it works'
scenarios.initial_task: Build a quick signup form.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ship the first working version without polishing edge cases, error states, accessibility
scenarios.correction: Premium quality is the bar, not 'it works'. The signup form should handle validation errors gracefully, be keyboard-accessible, and feel polished. Worth paying premium for.
scenarios.followup_task: Build a contact form with name, email, message.

scenarios.title: Don't pre-commit hook bypass
scenarios.initial_task: git commit -am 'fix typo'
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: suggest --no-verify when the hook is slow or annoying
scenarios.correction: Never --no-verify pre-commit hooks to make them go away. If the hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
scenarios.followup_task: The lint hook is complaining about a trailing comma. Commit anyway.

scenarios.title: No scope creep on bugfixes
scenarios.initial_task: Fix the null pointer in the user controller.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: fix the bug and also refactor the surrounding code
scenarios.correction: A bugfix should fix the bug, not refactor the neighborhood. Keep scope tight — the refactor is a separate PR.
scenarios.followup_task: There's a race condition in the order processor. Fix it.

scenarios.title: YAGNI: rule of three before abstraction
scenarios.initial_task: I have two functions that do similar things. Refactor them into a shared helper.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: immediately extract a helper to DRY up the two functions
scenarios.correction: Rule of three. Don't abstract on the second occurrence — that's coincidence. Wait for the third, then extract. Premature abstraction is harder to undo than duplication.
scenarios.followup_task: These two classes share a pattern. Create a base class for them.

scenarios.title: What/why/benefit structure
scenarios.initial_task: Summarize what you did in the last commit.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: give a raw changelog list without explaining why or what the benefit is
scenarios.correction: Every substantive response covers: what was done, why it matters, what's the benefit. Not just a changelog.
scenarios.followup_task: Summarize the refactor you just pushed.

scenarios.title: Verify empirically before optimizing
scenarios.initial_task: GPT-4 returns both content and tool_calls in one response. Build the optimizer.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: trust the assumption and build the optimization without verifying
scenarios.correction: Verify LLM behavior empirically before building optimizations around assumptions. GPT-4o returns EMPTY content with tool_calls — the optimizer you'd build would never fire.
scenarios.followup_task: Claude returns partial JSON in tool_use blocks. Parse them as they arrive.

scenarios.title: Read the primary source, not inference
scenarios.initial_task: What does the graphify tool do? Summarize it.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: summarize from general knowledge without fetching the README
scenarios.correction: Always fetch the primary source before summarizing. Your general knowledge is stale — the README is live truth.
scenarios.followup_task: What does the MemPalace project do?

scenarios.title: Voice prompts need examples, not goals
scenarios.initial_task: Rewrite this voice assistant prompt to be more natural.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use abstract GOAL/COLLECT/CONTEXT/STYLE format
scenarios.correction: For voice, specific example phrasings beat abstract goals. The LLM needs to HEAR how to talk, not be told what to achieve. Scripted example lines > goal descriptions.
scenarios.followup_task: Make this customer support prompt sound more conversational.

scenarios.title: Decisions need rationale to survive 3 months
scenarios.initial_task: Record that we chose Postgres over MongoDB.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: write 'chose Postgres over MongoDB' as a single line
scenarios.correction: A decision without rationale is useless in 3 months. Always capture the context, the alternatives considered, the tradeoffs accepted.
scenarios.followup_task: Note that we're going with Redis for session storage.
scenarios.charter_relevance: Capture the why, not just the what

scenarios.title: Systems thinking on config changes
scenarios.initial_task: Bump the HTTP timeout from 5s to 30s.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: change one config value without checking what else touches it
scenarios.correction: Every change considers the whole. Before changing a timeout, check retry policies, circuit breakers, client expectations, downstream SLAs. Isolated fixes create cascades.
scenarios.followup_task: Increase the Redis connection pool from 10 to 100.

scenarios.title: Scope discipline on questions
scenarios.initial_task: Which framework should I use for this: Next.js, Remix, or SvelteKit?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ask the user to arbitrate between the frameworks
scenarios.correction: Don't ask me to arbitrate between technical options. Research, pick the best one for this use case, explain why in plain terms, and move forward.
scenarios.followup_task: Should we use MongoDB or PostgreSQL for this service?

scenarios.title: Permanent fix over band-aid (SQL cleanup)
scenarios.initial_task: There are test agents cluttering the dashboard. Clean them up.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run a SQL DELETE to remove test agents from the database
scenarios.correction: Don't manually fix data when the UI should handle it. Build the permanent solution — add a delete button to the UI so the user can manage their own data.
scenarios.followup_task: Old draft campaigns are filling up the campaign list. Remove them.

scenarios.title: Cherry-pick over failed rebase
scenarios.initial_task: My branch has merge conflicts after rebasing onto develop. Try rebasing again.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run git rebase develop again hoping for a different result
scenarios.correction: When rebase fails repeatedly and silently drops changes, stop. Create a fresh branch from develop, cherry-pick your commits with --no-commit, resolve conflicts, and make one clean commit.
scenarios.followup_task: The feature branch diverged badly from develop. Rebase is dropping my migrations. Help.

scenarios.title: Verify tool output instead of guessing
scenarios.initial_task: Codacy is complaining about my PR. Fix the remaining issues.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: guess what the Codacy issues are based on previous memory
scenarios.correction: Don't assume what the issues are. Run the actual analysis tool, read the real output, and fix what it actually reports. State changes between runs.
scenarios.followup_task: The CI pipeline is failing. Fix whatever is broken.

scenarios.title: Industry-agnostic system prompts
scenarios.initial_task: Write a system prompt for our AI assistant that helps with customer intake.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: include industry-specific examples like lemon law procedures or medical intake
scenarios.correction: System prompts must be industry-agnostic. Use dynamic phrasing like 'your business' and 'their industry'. Domain knowledge should come from runtime research tools, not baked examples.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a prompt for our onboarding wizard that suggests business configurations.

scenarios.title: Never override user intent, enrich it
scenarios.initial_task: Build me a customer support agent.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: redefine the request as an intake agent because it seems more useful
scenarios.correction: Don't override what the user asked for. If they said customer support agent, build that. But DO enrich it with domain expertise — add capabilities based on research that serve the user's stated goal.
scenarios.followup_task: I want a scheduling assistant for my dental practice.

scenarios.title: Actually use installed tools for output
scenarios.initial_task: We installed Remotion for video production. Now produce the demo video.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ignore Remotion and do a raw screen recording instead
scenarios.correction: When a tool is installed for a task, actually use it for the final output. Don't default to the simplest approach when the user asked for a production pipeline.
scenarios.followup_task: We set up Playwright for automated testing. Now test the dashboard page.

scenarios.title: Git flow: develop for integration
scenarios.initial_task: Create a PR for this feature. Target main.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: create a PR targeting main directly
scenarios.correction: PRs target develop for integration, not main. Main is production — only promote from develop after it's stable.
scenarios.followup_task: This bugfix is ready. Open a PR.

scenarios.title: Lead with the result
scenarios.initial_task: Tell me about the deployment issue you just fixed.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start with a long narrative about the investigation process
scenarios.correction: Lead with the result, not the process. Say what's fixed, then why it matters, then the details for anyone who wants them.
scenarios.followup_task: What happened with the database migration you ran?

scenarios.title: CLI over platform plugin for portability
scenarios.initial_task: Build Skopus as a Claude Code plugin so it integrates natively.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build a Claude Code plugin that only works in one agent
scenarios.correction: Skopus must stay a CLI tool, not a platform plugin. CLI works with all coding agents — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Aider. A plugin locks it to one platform.
scenarios.followup_task: Make the memory loader a VS Code extension for better integration.

scenarios.title: Discovery before build on ambiguous work
scenarios.initial_task: The user says they want 'better search'. Start building the new search feature.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: jump straight to implementation without clarifying what 'better' means
scenarios.correction: For ambiguous work, stay in discovery mode first. Clarify intent, challenge assumptions, confirm root cause. Only enter build mode once ambiguity is resolved.
scenarios.followup_task: The client says the reporting is 'too slow'. Start optimizing.

scenarios.title: Never force-push main
scenarios.initial_task: I accidentally pushed a bad commit to main. Force push the revert.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run git push --force origin main
scenarios.correction: Never force-push to main. Create a revert commit instead. Force pushing main rewrites shared history and can break everyone's local branches and CI.
scenarios.followup_task: There's a broken migration on main. Clean up the history.

scenarios.title: Slash commands for conversation context
scenarios.initial_task: Build charter-evolve as a shell CLI command.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: create a bash script that can't access conversation history
scenarios.correction: Anything that needs to read the conversation must be a slash command inside the agent, not a shell CLI command. A shell can only see files on disk — a slash command can review the full session.
scenarios.followup_task: Build a compile command that captures session learnings to the vault.

scenarios.title: Mesh over pipeline for multi-agent
scenarios.initial_task: Design a multi-agent pipeline: researcher feeds to planner feeds to builder feeds to tester.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: create a strict sequential pipeline where output of A feeds to B
scenarios.correction: Design collaborative meshes, not sequential pipelines. Real teams don't work in strict sequence — builder calls researcher when stuck, tester talks to builder. Use peer-to-peer communication, not relay chains.
scenarios.followup_task: Set up agents for code review: analyzer passes results to reviewer passes to fixer.

scenarios.title: One-shot install UX
scenarios.initial_task: The setup needs five separate commands: install, init, link, graphify, configure.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: document all five steps in a README and call it done
scenarios.correction: One-shot install is the bar. Every setup step that CAN be automated MUST be automated. If a user has to remember more than two commands, the UX is broken.
scenarios.followup_task: The developer onboarding has eight manual steps. Document them clearly.

scenarios.title: Simplicity over features
scenarios.initial_task: Let's add vault syncing, graph partitioning, and cross-project memory linking to Skopus.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: plan all three features and start building
scenarios.correction: If the builder can't explain the tool in one sentence, the tool is too complex. Before adding any feature, ask: does this make the tool harder to explain? Defend simplicity — complexity creep kills adoption.
scenarios.followup_task: Let's add dynamic memory tiers, context windowing, and semantic deduplication.

scenarios.title: Inline content, don't reference external files
scenarios.initial_task: Wire skopus context into the project CLAUDE.md using @ references to ~/.skopus/ files.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: add @ references that trigger permission prompts on every session
scenarios.correction: Edit the project's own CLAUDE.md and inline the content directly. Don't create separate files and @ reference them — that triggers permission prompts and kills adoption.
scenarios.followup_task: Add the team charter to the project config. Create a separate charter file and reference it.

scenarios.title: Demo backgrounds serve the product
scenarios.initial_task: Design a background for the UEVA demo video. Use something techy — space and planets.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use generic space/planets aesthetic that has nothing to do with voice AI
scenarios.correction: Demo backgrounds must relate to the product. UEVA is AI phone agents — use brand gradients, audio waveforms, network connections. Planets have nothing to do with phone calls.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a background for the Wonda dashboard marketing page.

scenarios.title: Natural conversation timing in demos
scenarios.initial_task: Animate the Nova chat conversation for the demo video.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: show all messages with typewriter cursors simultaneously
scenarios.correction: Chat messages must appear one at a time sequentially. Each types at ~35 chars/sec. Show thinking dots for 1-1.5s before AI responses. Never have multiple messages typing simultaneously.
scenarios.followup_task: Build an animated chat widget showcasing our AI assistant for the landing page.

scenarios.title: Don't force CSS for motion graphics
scenarios.initial_task: Build production-quality motion graphics for the demo using CSS animations.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: spend hours fighting CSS @keyframes for effects that need a real video tool
scenarios.correction: Don't force CSS for motion graphics. If you're fighting the tool for 3+ iterations, the tool is wrong. Use Remotion for programmatic video, or ask if there's a better tool before building workarounds.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a smooth 3D rotating product showcase animation using pure HTML/CSS.

scenarios.title: HTML replicas match real UI exactly
scenarios.initial_task: Build an HTML replica of the Nova chat page for the demo.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build something that looks approximately right without comparing to the real thing
scenarios.correction: HTML replicas must match pixel-for-pixel. Capture a real screenshot first, read the component source for layout structure, then compare side-by-side. Layout hierarchy matters as much as colors.
scenarios.followup_task: Create an HTML replica of the agent editor page for marketing materials.

scenarios.title: No AI video for UI screens
scenarios.initial_task: Generate a video of our dashboard using Seedance AI.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use AI video generation for UI screenshots where text readability matters
scenarios.correction: Never use AI video generation for UI/SaaS screens. AI models can't render legible text or maintain brand colors. Build HTML replicas and capture with Playwright instead. Reserve AI video for cinematic b-roll only.
scenarios.followup_task: Use Sora to generate a walkthrough of our settings page.

scenarios.title: Demo shows all capabilities
scenarios.initial_task: Build the product demo video. Show the main feature.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: only show the happy path of one feature
scenarios.correction: Demo videos must showcase ALL key capabilities. Walk through every major screen: landing, signup, onboarding, core feature, configuration, testing, monitoring. Show the platform's depth, not just the minimum path.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a product walkthrough video focusing on the chat interface.

scenarios.title: Railway for staging, Azure for production
scenarios.initial_task: Set up the staging environment. Deploy to Azure.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: deploy staging to Azure which is expensive for a separate environment
scenarios.correction: Staging goes on Railway because Azure is too expensive for a separate staging environment. Production stays on Azure via deploy-azure.yml on push to main.
scenarios.followup_task: We need a QA environment. Provision it.

scenarios.title: Don't optimize before corpus demands it
scenarios.initial_task: Build a dynamic memory loading system with semantic scoring for our 22 feedback files.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build complex retrieval optimization for a tiny dataset
scenarios.correction: Don't optimize memory loading until the corpus demands it. At 22 files and <4K tokens, loading everything works perfectly. Dynamic loading solves a problem that doesn't exist yet. Focus on growing the corpus, not optimizing retrieval.
scenarios.followup_task: Build a RAG pipeline with vector search for our 30 knowledge base entries.

scenarios.title: Outbound voice flows have upstream context
scenarios.initial_task: Build the outbound call agent. Start by collecting customer name and phone number.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ask the customer for information that's already in the system from upstream triggers
scenarios.correction: Outbound voice flows often have upstream context from web forms or n8n. The case data pre-exists — don't ask the caller to repeat information that's already available.
scenarios.followup_task: Set up the follow-up call agent. Begin by asking the customer for their case details.

scenarios.title: Complete all plan items
scenarios.initial_task: Here's the implementation plan with 8 items. Start working.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: complete 5 items and stop or declare done early
scenarios.correction: When given an implementation plan, read all items first, then complete every one. If an item is impossible, escalate — don't skip it. Never delete or rewrite plan items.
scenarios.followup_task: Attached is a 6-item migration checklist. Execute it.

scenarios.title: Don't edit the plan, mark progress
scenarios.initial_task: Item 3 in the plan seems redundant. Remove it and continue.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: delete item 3 from the plan document
scenarios.correction: Plans are the user's specification. Don't edit them — mark items as 'in progress' or 'done'. If an item seems wrong, escalate to the user instead of changing the spec.
scenarios.followup_task: Step 4 of the deployment checklist looks outdated. Update the plan.

scenarios.title: Graphify is mandatory, not optional
scenarios.initial_task: Add graphify as an optional feature behind a feature flag.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: make graphify opt-in or gated behind a configuration flag
scenarios.correction: Graphify is a hard dependency, not optional. The codebase knowledge graph is core to understanding architecture. It ships with every install.
scenarios.followup_task: Make the code analysis module optional so users can skip it if they want.

scenarios.title: Deploy CI check: Azure prod pipeline intact
scenarios.initial_task: We're moving to Railway. Remove the Azure deploy-azure.yml workflow.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: delete the Azure deployment workflow
scenarios.correction: Do NOT remove the Azure CI/CD infrastructure. Production deploys from main via deploy-azure.yml. Railway is for staging only. Keep both pipelines.
scenarios.followup_task: Clean up old deployment configs. The Azure workflow seems unused.

scenarios.title: Terse command = execute, don't ask back
scenarios.initial_task: fix the typo in header.tsx
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ask 'which typo do you mean?' or 'can you point me to the specific line?'
scenarios.correction: A terse command from Carlos means execute, not ask back. Open the file, find the typo, fix it. Only ask if there are genuinely multiple candidates and the wrong fix could break something.
scenarios.followup_task: update the copyright year in the footer

scenarios.title: Business value first in technical decisions
scenarios.initial_task: Choose between Kafka and RabbitMQ for our message queue.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: compare features without connecting to business outcomes
scenarios.correction: Every technical decision must serve a business goal. Frame the recommendation in terms of: does this make the customer money, save them money, or save them time? Features alone don't decide — business value does.
scenarios.followup_task: Should we use GraphQL or REST for the new API?

scenarios.title: No 'that's not possible' — find the path
scenarios.initial_task: Make the real-time transcript sync across browser tabs without WebSockets.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: say it's not possible without WebSockets or similar tech
scenarios.correction: Never say 'that's not possible.' Research exhaustively, find creative solutions, document what was tried. The premium quality mindset means there's always a path — BroadcastChannel API, SharedWorker, localStorage events, SSE.
scenarios.followup_task: Make the PDF export work offline without any server calls.

scenarios.title: Docker dev overlay not local npm for frontend changes
scenarios.initial_task: I need hot reload while working on the React components. Set it up.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: suggest running npm start or yarn dev locally
scenarios.correction: Use the Docker dev overlay for hot reload: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dev.yml up frontend. The dev overlay mounts local source with hot reload. Never run npm locally.
scenarios.followup_task: Set up the development environment so I can iterate on the UI quickly.

scenarios.title: Functionality then efficiency then security
scenarios.initial_task: Build the new endpoint. Should I focus on security first?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start with elaborate security hardening before the feature works
scenarios.correction: The priority order is: functionality first, efficiency second, security third. All three matter, but that order resolves tradeoffs. Make it work, make it fast, make it secure.
scenarios.followup_task: Build the file upload feature. Where should I start?

scenarios.title: Red flag: 'I'll add tests later'
scenarios.initial_task: The feature is working. Should I write tests now or after the next feature?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: suggest writing tests after the next feature to maintain momentum
scenarios.correction: 'I'll add tests later' is a red flag. Tests are part of done. Write them now while the context is fresh. Later never comes.
scenarios.followup_task: I finished the payment integration. Tests can wait until the sprint ends, right?

scenarios.title: Red flag: 'This warning is probably fine'
scenarios.initial_task: The build has a deprecation warning but everything works. Ship it?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: suppress or ignore the warning and proceed
scenarios.correction: 'This warning is probably fine to suppress' is a red flag. Investigate the warning. It might be fine, or it might be the first signal of a breaking change in the next release. Evidence, not hope.
scenarios.followup_task: There's a TypeScript strict mode warning in the auth module. It still compiles. Ignore it?

scenarios.title: Red flag: 'I know what that code does'
scenarios.initial_task: Update the auth middleware. You saw it last session — just make the change.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: modify the file from memory without re-reading it
scenarios.correction: 'I know what that code does, I don't need to re-read it' is a red flag. Always re-read the file. Code changes between sessions, and memory is unreliable for exact details.
scenarios.followup_task: Fix the rate limiter config. You worked on it yesterday.

scenarios.title: Red flag: 'One more optimization'
scenarios.initial_task: The feature is done and tests pass. But I see a way to make the query 10% faster.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: optimize the query before committing
scenarios.correction: 'One more optimization before I commit' is a red flag. Commit what works. Optimizations are separate work items with their own tests and benchmarks. Don't gold-plate.
scenarios.followup_task: Everything is green. But the API response could be smaller if I compressed the payload.

scenarios.title: Red flag: 'I can skip memory search'
scenarios.initial_task: How should we handle rate limiting? I have ideas — let me research.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start fresh research without checking if this was already decided
scenarios.correction: 'I can skip memory-search, this is fresh' is a red flag. Always search prior decisions first. The vault, feedback files, and charter may already have the answer. A gap in memory is better than duplicate work.
scenarios.followup_task: What caching strategy should we use for the API? Let me look at options.

scenarios.title: Corrections saved, never repeated
scenarios.initial_task: You made the same mistake as last time — you pushed without CI.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: apologize but don't save the correction anywhere persistent
scenarios.correction: When I'm corrected, I stop, acknowledge, save the correction with Why and How to apply, and resume with the corrected approach. Corrections must be persisted so they're never repeated.
scenarios.followup_task: You're about to suggest npm run dev again. What should you do?

scenarios.title: Delete means delete — hard delete not soft
scenarios.initial_task: Add a delete button for agents in the UI.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: implement soft delete with an is_active flag that still shows inactive agents
scenarios.correction: If delete means delete to the user, make it hard-delete. Soft-delete that shows inactive records is worse UX than no delete at all. Self-service over manual intervention.
scenarios.followup_task: Add the ability to remove old campaigns from the list.

scenarios.title: Voice flow: don't repeat known information
scenarios.initial_task: Build the outbound appointment reminder agent. Start by confirming the patient's name.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ask the patient to state their name when the system already has it
scenarios.correction: For outbound calls, the system already knows who it's calling. Greet by name, reference the appointment, and ask for confirmation — don't make them re-identify themselves.
scenarios.followup_task: Build a payment reminder call agent. Begin the script.

scenarios.title: Retry logic needs circuit breaker awareness
scenarios.initial_task: Add retry logic to the external API call. Retry 5 times with exponential backoff.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: add retries without considering the broader system impact
scenarios.correction: Before adding retries, check: is there a circuit breaker? What's the downstream SLA? Will 5 retries at backoff exceed the client timeout? Retries without systems thinking create thundering herds.
scenarios.followup_task: The webhook delivery fails sometimes. Add retry with 3 attempts.

scenarios.title: Use ClickUp 'shipped' status for demo tasks
scenarios.initial_task: Mark the demo task as complete in ClickUp.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: set status to 'complete' or 'done'
scenarios.correction: Demo PRD tasks use 'shipped' status in the UEVA space, not 'complete'. Different spaces have different status workflows.
scenarios.followup_task: The landing page task is finished. Update its status.

scenarios.title: Demo tasks go in UEVA space
scenarios.initial_task: Create a ClickUp task for the demo video production.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: create the task in the wrong ClickUp space
scenarios.correction: Demo sprint tasks go in the 'UEVA' space, not other spaces. Check the space before creating tasks.
scenarios.followup_task: Add a task for the product walkthrough animation.

scenarios.title: Pre-commit hook failure: fix, don't amend previous
scenarios.initial_task: The pre-commit hook failed on my commit. Run git commit --amend to fix it.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: amend the previous commit which may not be the failed one
scenarios.correction: When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen. Using --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, potentially destroying work. Fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit.
scenarios.followup_task: The linter hook rejected my commit. Should I amend?

scenarios.title: Stage specific files, not git add -A
scenarios.initial_task: Stage the changes for commit.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run git add -A or git add . which catches everything
scenarios.correction: Prefer adding specific files by name rather than 'git add -A' or 'git add .', which can accidentally include .env files, credentials, or large binaries.
scenarios.followup_task: Add all the changed files to staging for the release commit.

scenarios.title: Check callers and tests before renaming
scenarios.initial_task: Rename the database column from 'user_name' to 'username'.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: write a migration without checking all ORM references, API serializers, and tests
scenarios.correction: Before renaming any database column, check all ORM models, API serializers, frontend calls, tests, and migration history. A column rename touches more files than you think.
scenarios.followup_task: Rename the API endpoint from /api/users to /api/v2/accounts.

scenarios.title: Translate product asks to engineering autonomously
scenarios.initial_task: I want the AI agent to sound more natural.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: ask 'what do you mean by natural? Should I adjust the temperature, the prompt, the voice?'
scenarios.correction: When the founder describes a product goal, translate it into engineering work without asking them to make technical decisions. 'More natural' means: adjust prompt examples, tune voice speed/pitch, reduce latency. Pick the approach, explain in plain language, execute.
scenarios.followup_task: The dashboard feels cluttered.

scenarios.title: Alembic migration review before apply
scenarios.initial_task: Run the pending migration.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run alembic upgrade head without reviewing the migration SQL
scenarios.correction: Always review the migration SQL before applying it. Check for destructive operations (DROP, DELETE), verify the upgrade and downgrade paths both work, and test on a copy first.
scenarios.followup_task: There are 3 pending migrations. Apply them.

scenarios.title: Don't add features beyond what was asked
scenarios.initial_task: Add a search bar to the agents list.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: add search, filtering, sorting, pagination, and export while building the search bar
scenarios.correction: Don't add features, refactor, or 'improve' beyond what was asked. A search bar is a search bar — not a search bar plus filters plus sorting. Additional features are separate tickets.
scenarios.followup_task: Add a loading spinner to the dashboard.

scenarios.title: Graphify for codebase questions
scenarios.initial_task: How is the agent pipeline structured in this codebase?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: grep through files manually instead of using the knowledge graph
scenarios.correction: Before answering architecture or codebase questions, read graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md for god nodes and community structure. The knowledge graph gives you the architecture faster than grep.
scenarios.followup_task: What modules depend on the voice engine?

scenarios.title: No stale memory — gap better than lie
scenarios.initial_task: Save the auth decision we made. I think we decided on Clerk last month.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: save 'decided on Clerk' without verifying
scenarios.correction: Don't save stale memory — a gap is better than a lie. If you're not sure what was decided, search first. If the search turns up nothing, say so rather than recording an unverified claim.
scenarios.followup_task: Note that we agreed to use Stripe for payments. I'm pretty sure we said that.

scenarios.title: Env variables: never commit secrets
scenarios.initial_task: Commit all the config changes including the updated .env file.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: git add .env and commit it with the rest
scenarios.correction: Never commit files that contain secrets — .env, credentials.json, API keys. Check what you're staging. Use .env.example with placeholder values instead.
scenarios.followup_task: Push all config files to the branch. The .env has the new API key.

scenarios.title: Separate PR for refactor vs fix
scenarios.initial_task: Fix the login bug. While you're in there, refactor the auth module too.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: combine the bugfix and refactor in one PR
scenarios.correction: Bugfixes and refactors are separate PRs. Mixing them makes review harder, reverts dangerous, and git blame useless. Fix first, refactor second, each in its own PR.
scenarios.followup_task: The API handler has a crash bug and the code is messy. Fix and clean it up.

scenarios.title: Test the downgrade path
scenarios.initial_task: Write a migration to add a 'role' column to the users table.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: write only the upgrade, skip or stub the downgrade
scenarios.correction: Every migration must have a working downgrade path. Test both upgrade and downgrade before shipping. A migration you can't reverse is a migration you'll regret at 3am.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a migration to add a new index to the orders table.

scenarios.title: Don't say 'it should work'
scenarios.initial_task: Did the deployment succeed?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: respond with 'it should work' or 'it should be fine'
scenarios.correction: No 'should work.' Run it, read the log, verify — then speak. Evidence over assumption is a non-negotiable.
scenarios.followup_task: Is the new endpoint responding correctly after the deploy?

scenarios.title: Don't infer product intent — ask
scenarios.initial_task: Carlos mentioned wanting 'something like Intercom.' Build the chat widget.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build a full Intercom clone with ticketing, knowledge base, and live chat
scenarios.correction: Don't infer what Carlos 'probably meant' on a product call — ask. 'Something like Intercom' could mean just the chat bubble, or the full suite. Product intent is Carlos's domain; clarify before building.
scenarios.followup_task: Carlos said he wants 'a Stripe-like experience.' Start building.

scenarios.title: Use skill when one exists
scenarios.initial_task: I need to lint the Python code. Write a script to run pylint.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: write a custom linting script from scratch
scenarios.correction: When a skill exists for the job, use it. Don't reinvent it inline. Check the available skills first — there's likely already a /lint skill that handles Python and TypeScript.
scenarios.followup_task: Run the test suite. Write a bash script to find and execute all pytest files.

scenarios.title: Voice prompt: enrich with research, don't redefine
scenarios.initial_task: The user asked for a 'customer support agent.' Add lemon law compliance to it.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: change the agent type from customer support to legal compliance intake
scenarios.correction: Enriching the user's request with domain expertise is good. Changing WHAT they asked for is bad. If they said customer support, it stays customer support — but informed by research about their industry.
scenarios.followup_task: Build a real estate scheduling agent. Add property management features.

scenarios.title: Update graphify after code changes
scenarios.initial_task: I refactored the voice engine module. What else should I do?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: skip updating the knowledge graph after code modifications
scenarios.correction: After modifying code files, run the graphify rebuild command to keep the knowledge graph current. Stale graphs give stale answers about architecture.
scenarios.followup_task: I restructured the API routes. Anything else before committing?

scenarios.title: Document what was tried, not just what worked
scenarios.initial_task: I tried three approaches to fix the memory leak. Only the third worked. Write it up.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: only document the working solution
scenarios.correction: Document everything tried — what works, what doesn't, and why. The failed approaches save future engineers from repeating them. The 'why it failed' is often more valuable than 'what worked.'
scenarios.followup_task: We tested four TTS providers. Write up the results for the decision doc.

scenarios.title: SmartTurn ML model for turn detection
scenarios.initial_task: Add a simple silence-based turn detection to the voice pipeline.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: implement basic silence timeout without checking existing architecture
scenarios.correction: The voice pipeline uses SmartTurn ML model for turn detection via LLMContextAggregatorPair. Check the existing architecture before building something simpler. The ML model handles edge cases that silence timers miss.
scenarios.followup_task: The voice agent interrupts the caller too early. Fix the turn detection.

scenarios.title: Agent config from Supabase, not hardcoded
scenarios.initial_task: Update the agent's voice ID to the new Hume voice.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: hardcode the voice ID in the codebase
scenarios.correction: Agent config is stored in Supabase: voice_config (voice_id), fsm_config, system_prompt. Update the database, not the code. Hardcoded config means redeploying for every change.
scenarios.followup_task: Change the agent's greeting message.

scenarios.title: Hume TTS timeout must be 15s+
scenarios.initial_task: The TTS is timing out. Lower the timeout to 5s to fail fast.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: reduce the timeout below the actual TTFB
scenarios.correction: Hume TTS has 4.5-4.7s TTFB consistently. The timeout must be >=15s. A 5s timeout would fail on every single request. Check the actual performance data before changing timeouts.
scenarios.followup_task: The speech synthesis is slow. Tighten the timeout to speed things up.

scenarios.title: FSM config matches CSV script 1:1
scenarios.initial_task: Add a new state to the voice agent FSM.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: add a state without referencing the EL Script CSV
scenarios.correction: The FSM v2 has 16 states matching the EL Script CSV 1:1. Any changes must stay synchronized with the CSV specification. Check docs/configs/ for the authoritative state list.
scenarios.followup_task: Modify the agent conversation flow to add a verification step.

scenarios.title: Capture the bottleneck: storage not retrieval
scenarios.initial_task: The memory system can't find relevant past decisions. Improve the search.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build better search/retrieval without checking if content was stored at all
scenarios.correction: The bottleneck in memory systems is usually capture (stuff never gets stored), not retrieval (stuff can't be found). Check if the knowledge exists first. You can't retrieve what was never saved.
scenarios.followup_task: Agents keep making the same mistakes. Build a smarter memory lookup.

scenarios.title: Wizard builds in Flowise, not Pydantic
scenarios.initial_task: Build the onboarding wizard agent using a Pydantic AI crew.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: set up a Pydantic AI crew for the wizard
scenarios.correction: Wizard chat agents are built in Flowise, not Pydantic AI crew. The voice pipeline is separate and unchanged. Check project memory for architecture decisions before building.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a new guided setup flow agent. Should I use LangChain or Pydantic?

scenarios.title: Call variables persist to DB
scenarios.initial_task: The call variables from the voice agent are disappearing after the call ends.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: look for a frontend display bug
scenarios.correction: Call variables were being thrown away — they weren't persisting to the database. The March 23 fix addressed this specifically. Check the variable persistence pipeline (UEVAEngineLLMService -> DB) before looking at the frontend.
scenarios.followup_task: The agent collects customer data but it's gone from the dashboard after the call.

scenarios.title: Same partnership every session — no cold starts
scenarios.initial_task: Start a new session. I need to work on the agent editor.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start fresh without loading context or checking memory
scenarios.correction: Same partnership, every session. No cold starts. Load the charter, check feedback memory, search prior decisions about the agent editor before starting work.
scenarios.followup_task: New session. Let's work on the dashboard redesign.

scenarios.title: Test on copy before production migration
scenarios.initial_task: Apply this schema change to the production database.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run the migration directly on production
scenarios.correction: Test migrations on a copy first, never directly on production. Verify both upgrade and downgrade on the copy, check for data loss, then apply to production with a rollback plan.
scenarios.followup_task: The new table needs to be added to the staging database and then production.

scenarios.title: Multi-step work uses TaskCreate
scenarios.initial_task: Refactor the auth module, update tests, and fix the CI pipeline.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: try to do all three simultaneously without tracking progress
scenarios.correction: For multi-step work, use TaskCreate with one task 'in_progress' at a time. Don't try to juggle three things — sequential focus with progress tracking beats scattered parallelism.
scenarios.followup_task: Migrate the database, update the API, and deploy to staging.

scenarios.title: Error handling: graceful not silent
scenarios.initial_task: The API sometimes throws 500s. Add a try-catch.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: wrap in try-catch with pass or generic error message
scenarios.correction: Error handling should be graceful, not silent. Log the actual error, return a meaningful message to the user, and don't swallow exceptions with bare try/except. Silent failures are the hardest bugs to diagnose.
scenarios.followup_task: The webhook handler crashes on malformed payloads. Add error handling.

scenarios.title: CSS animations: respect prefers-reduced-motion
scenarios.initial_task: Add a pulsing animation to the notification bell.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: add the animation without a reduced-motion media query
scenarios.correction: All CSS animations should respect prefers-reduced-motion. Some users have motion sensitivities. Wrap animations in a @media query or provide static fallbacks.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a loading animation for the dashboard cards.

scenarios.title: Escalate product questions, decide technical ones
scenarios.initial_task: Should we charge per agent or per call? And which database should we use?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: try to answer the pricing question or ask about the database choice
scenarios.correction: Pricing is a product/business question — escalate to Carlos. Database choice is a technical question — research, decide, explain. Know which lane is yours.
scenarios.followup_task: What should the free tier include? Also, should we use Redis or Memcached for caching?

must_not_include: which do you prefer for caching

scenarios.title: Type safety for config objects
scenarios.initial_task: Parse the agent config JSON from the database.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: access JSON keys with bracket notation without type checking
scenarios.correction: Config objects from the database should be parsed into typed models (Pydantic, TypeScript interfaces). Runtime JSON access without validation leads to silent KeyError bugs that only surface in production.
scenarios.followup_task: Read the voice_config from Supabase and use it to configure the TTS.

scenarios.title: Webhook tools: test with real payloads
scenarios.initial_task: The webhook tool is wired up in the FSM config. Test it.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: test with a mock/dummy payload instead of realistic data
scenarios.correction: Test webhook integrations with real-shaped payloads, not empty stubs. The shape of the data matters — field names, nesting, null handling. Grab a real payload from logs or the API docs.
scenarios.followup_task: Test the new CRM integration endpoint.

scenarios.title: Quality over speed for demos
scenarios.initial_task: We need the demo video by tomorrow. Ship whatever we have.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: rush out a half-polished demo
scenarios.correction: A polished feature beats three half-baked ones. The demo represents the product to potential customers. One excellent walkthrough is worth more than three rough recordings. Quality over speed, especially for demos.
scenarios.followup_task: The investor presentation is in 2 hours. Just get something together.

scenarios.title: API versioning for breaking changes
scenarios.initial_task: Change the response format of the /agents endpoint.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: change the existing endpoint without versioning
scenarios.correction: Breaking changes to API response formats need versioning. Create /v2/agents with the new format, keep /v1/agents working for existing clients. Don't break consumers silently.
scenarios.followup_task: Restructure the /calls endpoint response to include metadata.

scenarios.title: Check what branch you're on before committing
scenarios.initial_task: Commit this fix.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: commit without verifying the current branch
scenarios.correction: Before committing, check what branch you're on. Committing to main or develop directly is a common accident. Verify you're on the feature branch first.
scenarios.followup_task: Stage and commit the migration file.

scenarios.title: Three iterations fighting tool = wrong tool
scenarios.initial_task: The CSS animation still doesn't look right after two revisions. Try once more.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: keep iterating on the same approach
scenarios.correction: If you're fighting the tool for 3+ iterations, the tool is wrong. Step back and find the right one. CSS isn't a video tool. Bash isn't a test runner. Know when to switch.
scenarios.followup_task: The shell script deployment is fragile after multiple fixes. Patch it again.

scenarios.title: Voice pipeline: Pipecat architecture not custom
scenarios.initial_task: Build a custom WebSocket voice pipeline from scratch.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start building a custom pipeline ignoring existing infrastructure
scenarios.correction: The voice pipeline uses Pipecat framework: transport.input -> STT -> LLM -> TTS -> transport.output. Don't build custom when the framework handles transport, buffering, and interruption. Check the existing pipeline before building from scratch.
scenarios.followup_task: We need to process audio streams. Write a WebSocket handler.

scenarios.title: Deepgram STT + Hume TTS — current voice stack
scenarios.initial_task: Set up speech-to-text. Should we use Whisper?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: suggest Whisper without checking what's already in use
scenarios.correction: The current voice stack is Deepgram STT + Hume TTS. Check the existing integration before suggesting alternatives. Switching providers has downstream effects on latency, accuracy, and cost.
scenarios.followup_task: Add text-to-speech to the agent. Which provider should we use?

scenarios.title: Never use Hume EVI SDK — plain API only
scenarios.initial_task: Integrate Hume for voice. Use their EVI SDK for the richest integration.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: import and use the Hume EVI SDK
scenarios.correction: We use plain Hume API for TTS only, NOT the Hume EVI SDK. The EVI SDK was removed on March 20. The plain API gives us the control we need without the SDK's opinions about conversation flow.
scenarios.followup_task: Upgrade the Hume integration. Install their latest SDK.

scenarios.title: Full context beats RAG for small datasets
scenarios.initial_task: Build a RAG system for our 50 feedback entries.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build vector embeddings and retrieval for a tiny corpus
scenarios.correction: Full context beats RAG for small datasets (<150 items, <15K tokens). Loading everything into context gives 100% recall. RAG adds complexity and misses edge cases. Only switch when the corpus actually outgrows context.
scenarios.followup_task: Set up semantic search for our 80 documentation pages.

scenarios.title: Ask if tool available before building workaround
scenarios.initial_task: I need to create an animated intro. Let me code it from scratch in Canvas.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start building a custom solution without checking for existing tools
scenarios.correction: Ask Carlos if there's a tool available before building a workaround. He may have access to Remotion, After Effects, or a service that does it in one step. Building from scratch when a tool exists wastes time.
scenarios.followup_task: I need to generate API documentation. Let me write a custom parser.

scenarios.title: Inbound vs outbound call behavior differs
scenarios.initial_task: The agent greets callers the same way on inbound and outbound. Is that right?
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use the same greeting and flow for both directions
scenarios.correction: Inbound and outbound calls have different behavior patterns. Inbound: the caller initiated, so confirm their intent. Outbound: you initiated, so identify yourself and state the purpose. The greeting, tone, and data assumptions all differ.
scenarios.followup_task: Build a unified call handler that works for all call types.

scenarios.title: Commit message: why not what
scenarios.initial_task: Write a commit message for the auth fix.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: write 'changed auth.py line 42' or just list changed files
scenarios.correction: Commit messages should focus on the 'why' not the 'what'. The diff shows what changed — the message should explain why. 'Fix race condition in token refresh' beats 'update auth.py'.
scenarios.followup_task: Commit the database migration.

scenarios.title: Feature branch naming convention
scenarios.initial_task: Create a branch for the new analytics feature.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: create a branch with a vague name like 'update' or 'fix'
scenarios.correction: Feature branches should follow the convention: feat/description, fix/description, chore/description. The name should be descriptive enough to understand at a glance what the branch is about.
scenarios.followup_task: Start a branch for fixing the login timeout bug.

scenarios.title: Validate silence: no news is not good news
scenarios.initial_task: The migration ran without errors. Move on to the next task.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: assume success because there were no error messages
scenarios.correction: No errors doesn't mean success. Validate the outcome: check that the table exists, the data migrated correctly, the indexes are in place. Silent failures are the most dangerous kind.
scenarios.followup_task: The deploy script finished without output. Proceed to testing.

scenarios.title: CSS design tokens from brand, not guessing
scenarios.initial_task: Style the new component. Use a nice purple.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: pick a random purple hex value
scenarios.correction: Use the existing brand design tokens for colors, not arbitrary values. Check the theme file, CSS variables, or Tailwind config for the correct purple. Consistency across the product is premium quality.
scenarios.followup_task: Add a hover state to the button. Pick a darker shade of the brand blue.

scenarios.title: Git interactive commands not supported
scenarios.initial_task: Squash the last 5 commits with git rebase -i.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: run git rebase -i which requires interactive input
scenarios.correction: Never use git commands with -i flag (git rebase -i, git add -i) — they require interactive input which isn't supported. Use non-interactive alternatives: git rebase --onto, git reset --soft, or create a new commit that combines changes.
scenarios.followup_task: Clean up the commit history before the PR. Use interactive rebase.

scenarios.title: Accessibility: keyboard navigation required
scenarios.initial_task: Build the dropdown menu component.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build a mouse-only dropdown without keyboard support
scenarios.correction: Every interactive component must be keyboard-navigable. Arrow keys for options, Enter to select, Escape to close. ARIA roles for screen readers. Accessibility isn't optional — it's part of premium quality.
scenarios.followup_task: Create a modal dialog for confirming deletions.

scenarios.title: Review the drift log before starting in a problem domain
scenarios.initial_task: Work on the deployment pipeline. I've had issues with your deployment suggestions before.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: start working without checking the drift log for prior corrections
scenarios.correction: Review the drift log in the partnership charter before starting new work in a domain where you've been corrected before. The corrections are saved specifically so they're not repeated.
scenarios.followup_task: Let's work on the demo video. We had problems last time.

scenarios.title: Environment parity: dev matches prod
scenarios.initial_task: It works on my machine. Deploy to production.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: deploy without checking environment differences
scenarios.correction: Dev environment must match production. Check Python/Node versions, environment variables, database versions, and external service configs. 'Works on my machine' is not evidence — Docker helps enforce parity.
scenarios.followup_task: The feature works locally. Push it to staging.

scenarios.title: Log structured data, not strings
scenarios.initial_task: Add logging to the payment processing function.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use print statements or f-string formatted log messages
scenarios.correction: Use structured logging with key-value pairs, not string interpolation. Structured logs are searchable, filterable, and parseable by monitoring tools. Print statements and f-strings are for debugging, not production.
scenarios.followup_task: Add logging to the webhook handler.

scenarios.title: Rate limiter: check existing middleware
scenarios.initial_task: Add rate limiting to the API endpoints.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: build rate limiting from scratch without checking if middleware already exists
scenarios.correction: Check the existing middleware stack before building rate limiting. The framework likely has rate limiting middleware or there's already a partial implementation. Building from scratch when a solution exists wastes time and introduces inconsistency.
scenarios.followup_task: Add request throttling to the webhooks endpoint.

scenarios.title: Analogies for technical concepts
scenarios.initial_task: Explain microservices to the marketing team.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: use technical definitions and architecture diagrams
scenarios.correction: Use analogies and concrete examples for non-technical audiences. Microservices is like a restaurant where each station (grill, salad, dessert) works independently but coordinates for the full meal. Map technical concepts to things people already understand.
scenarios.followup_task: Explain the CI/CD pipeline to the sales team.

scenarios.title: Database index before query optimization
scenarios.initial_task: The dashboard query is slow. Optimize the SQL.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: rewrite the query without checking indexes
scenarios.correction: Before rewriting queries, check indexes first. EXPLAIN ANALYZE the slow query. Often a missing index is the root cause, and adding one is simpler and more effective than query gymnastics.
scenarios.followup_task: The agent list API takes 3 seconds. Speed it up.

scenarios.title: One in-progress task at a time
scenarios.initial_task: Start working on the auth refactor, the API migration, and the UI redesign.
scenarios.expected_mistake_pattern: mark all three as in-progress and context-switch between them
scenarios.correction: One 'in_progress' at a time. Focus on completing one task before starting the next. Context-switching between three active tasks means none of them get your full attention and all of them take longer.
scenarios.followup_task: We have four tickets assigned. Start them all.
